statement: In the $xy$-plane, the line $y = (k - 1)x + 3$ is perpendicular to the line $4x - 2y = 7$. What is the value of $k$?

choices.misconception: I changed the sign of the slope 2 but did not take its reciprocal, so I solved $k - 1 = -2$.
I took the reciprocal of the slope 2 but forgot to change its sign, so I solved $k - 1 = \tfrac{1}{2}$.
I set the slopes equal, $k - 1 = 2$, which is the condition for parallel lines, not perpendicular ones.

hints: Perpendicular lines have slopes whose product is $-1$. Find the slope of $4x - 2y = 7$ first.
Solving $4x - 2y = 7$ for $y$ gives $y = 2x - \tfrac{7}{2}$, so its slope is $2$. The other line has slope $k - 1$.
A line perpendicular to a line of slope $2$ has slope $-\tfrac{1}{2}$, so $k - 1 = -\tfrac{1}{2}$.

solutions.reliable: Solving $4x - 2y = 7$ for $y$ gives $y = 2x - \tfrac{7}{2}$, so its slope is $2$. The line $y = (k - 1)x + 3$ has slope $k - 1$. Perpendicular slopes multiply to $-1$, so $2(k - 1) = -1$, which gives $k - 1 = -\tfrac{1}{2}$ and $k = \tfrac{1}{2}$. Check: the slope is then $\tfrac{1}{2} - 1 = -\tfrac{1}{2}$, and $2 \cdot \left(-\tfrac{1}{2}\right) = -1$.
